paper.title_en: The Population of Radio Hypernebulae from Mass-Transferring Massive Binaries
paper.abstract_en: Massive binary evolution is punctuated by brief phases of highly super-Eddington mass transfer (MT) onto neutron stars and black holes, presaging luminous transients such as supernovae, common envelope events, and gravitational wave sources. These hyper-accreting phases power relativistic jets and slower mass-loaded outflows, inflating extended nebulae of relativistic particles. Though observed in the local universe as ultra-luminous X-ray binaries and micro-quasars, the present census is biased against shorter-lived and hence rarer but potentially even more extreme MT systems: so-called ``hypernebulae'' (HNbe). We use the binary population synthesis code (\textsc{COMPAS}) to estimate the MT population, which spans a wide range of MT rates $\dot{M} \sim 10^{2-7}\,\dot{M}_{\rm Edd}$ and source lifetimes $t_{\rm acc} \sim 10^{0-6}$ years. Combining this synthetic population with a semi-analytic model for their time-dependent radio emission, we predict the observable properties of HNbe over cosmic time. HNbe exhibit a broad GHz luminosity range extending to $L_{ν, \rm peak} \sim 10^{28-30}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$, and up to $\sim 10^{2}$ ($\sim 10^{5}$) HNbe are detectable by the wide-field radio surveys VLASS (DSA-2000) in our conservative model. A fraction of these systems should possess angular sizes and spatial offsets from star-forming regions (due to the first supernova kick) resolvable by VLBI. The most luminous donors, helium Hertzsprung-gap stars, may be detectable coincident with radio HNbe with Roman imaging out to distances $\sim 30$\,Mpc. Our findings suggest HNbe as promising probes of the pathways linking massive binaries to energetic transients.
